newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Air Liberte sheds flights.
newsitem.headline: French Air Liberte sheds flights.

text.p: French airline Air Liberte, placed under legal administration after defaulting on payments, said on Thursday it was withdrawing Airbus airliners from its fleet and cutting flights.
The private carrier said its Airbus-operated international routes Toulouse-Dakar and Bordeaux-Abidjan would be suspended from October 7, and its Paris-Montreal flight from November 2.
Domestic flights Paris-Montpellier and Bordeaux-Nice would be suspended from Tuesday
Passengers who had already bought tickets for these flights would be transferred to other airlines or get their money back.
Air Liberte, which was given last week six months to try and haul itself out of trouble, has drawn up a salvage plan shedding 285 jobs and focusing on medium- and short-haul flights.
Staff have agreed at an annual meeting to put two months' wages towards a capital increase to try to put the carrier back on course.
The airline has said the planned capital increase would be to the tune of 100 million francs, of which 60 percent would come from staff
